segments.text: And Job continued his discourse:
“How I long for the months gone by, for the days when God watched over me,
segments.speaker: Job

segments.text: when His lamp shone above my head, and by His light I walked through the darkness,
segments.speaker: Job

segments.text: when I was in my prime, when the friendship of God rested on my tent,
segments.speaker: Job

footnotes.text: + Hebrew in the time of my harvest

segments.text: when the Almighty was still with me and my children were around me,
segments.speaker: Job

segments.text: when my steps were bathed in cream and the rock poured out for me streams of oil!
segments.speaker: Job

segments.text: When I went out to the city gate and took my seat in the public square,
segments.speaker: Job

segments.text: the young men saw me and withdrew, and the old men rose to their feet.
segments.speaker: Job

segments.text: The princes refrained from speaking and covered their mouths with their hands.
segments.speaker: Job

segments.text: The voices of the nobles were hushed, and their tongues stuck to the roofs of their mouths.
segments.speaker: Job

segments.text: For those who heard me called me blessed, and those who saw me commended me,
segments.speaker: Job

segments.text: because I rescued the poor who cried out and the fatherless who had no helper.
segments.speaker: Job

segments.text: The dying man blessed me, and I made the widow’s heart sing for joy.
segments.speaker: Job

segments.text: I put on righteousness, and it clothed me; justice was my robe and my turban.
segments.speaker: Job

segments.text: I served as eyes to the blind and as feet to the lame.
segments.speaker: Job

segments.text: I was a father to the needy, and I took up the case of the stranger.
segments.speaker: Job

segments.text: I shattered the fangs of the unjust and snatched the prey from his teeth.
segments.speaker: Job

segments.text: So I thought: ‘I will die in my nest and multiply my days as the sand.
segments.speaker: Job

segments.text: My roots will spread out to the waters, and the dew will rest nightly on my branches.
segments.speaker: Job

segments.text: My glory is ever new within me, and my bow is renewed in my hand.’
segments.speaker: Job

segments.text: Men listened to me with expectation, waiting silently for my counsel.
segments.speaker: Job

segments.text: After my words, they spoke no more; my speech settled on them like dew.
segments.speaker: Job

segments.text: They waited for me as for rain and drank in my words like spring showers.
segments.speaker: Job

segments.text: If I smiled at them, they did not believe it; the light of my countenance was precious.
segments.speaker: Job

segments.text:
I chose their course and presided as chief. So I dwelt as a king among his troops,
as a comforter of the mourners.
segments.speaker: Job
